items.text: `make run-staging` starts the gateway + mock upstreams; a request with a valid JWT reaches the upstream; without it gets 401; the 11th request in a second gets 429.
Editing `config/tenants/lumen-pay.yaml` is picked up without restart; a broken edit is rejected and the previous config keeps serving.

`gwlint validate examples/lumen-pay.bad.yaml` exits 1 and names each violation with a line number and a fix; `gwlint --fix` produces a file that then passes except for the rules that need a human, which are listed.
`gwlint validate examples/lumen-pay.good.yaml` exits 0.
All tests pass; the README quick start works as written.
Stack: Go. (gateway and gwlint: one Go module, static binaries)
**Routing:** by host, path prefix and method to named upstreams; path rewrite.

**Multi-tenant config:** `config/gateway.yaml` (global) + `config/tenants/<tenant>.yaml` (one per onboarded customer). **Hot reload:** watch the directory; validate the new set; swap atomically; keep the last good config on error and log why.

**Authentication per route:** JWT/OAuth2 (issuer, audience, required scopes, JWKS URL with caching), API keys (hashed in config, never plaintext), optional mTLS client certificates. A route with no auth is a configuration error unless explicitly `public: true` with a reason.
**Rate limiting:** token bucket per tenant and per route (requests/second + burst).
**CORS** per route; **request size limits**; **request validation** against a JSON Schema or OpenAPI fragment per route.
**Resilience:** upstream timeouts, retries with backoff for idempotent methods, a simple circuit breaker.
**Headers:** add/remove/rename; propagate a request id.
**Observability:** structured JSON access logs with PII redaction (configurable field list), `/healthz`, `/readyz`, Prometheus `/metrics`.

**Two environments:** `staging` and `production` are two instances of the same binary with different config directories and ports. Provide `docker-compose.yml` for both plus two tiny mock upstreams so demos run end to end. (Do not depend on anything external.)
**Tests:** unit tests for routing, auth, rate limits, reload; an integration test that boots the gateway with the sample config and exercises a request through auth → rate limit → upstream.
A reverse-proxy API gateway, one static binary, configured by YAML.
**JSON Schema** for `tenants/<tenant>.yaml` (tenant id, owner + contact, tier, routes, auth, limits, CORS, upstreams, deprecation).
**A rulebook, in YAML, readable by non-engineers:** `rules/api-guidelines.yaml`. Each rule has `id`, `severity` (error|warn), `title`, `why`, `fix`. At least 20 rules:

**Security:** every route has auth (or an explicit, justified `public`); no wildcard CORS origin together with credentials; upstreams must be `https://`; no secrets inlined (detect API-key/JWT/password-shaped values); rate limits present and within bounds; no `/admin`, `/internal`, `/debug` paths exposed; JWT `audience` set; mTLS required for `tier: partner-sensitive`; request size capped; PII fields declared for redaction; no `*` methods.

**API guidelines:** versioned base path (`/v1/...`); kebab-case path segments; only allowed methods; timeouts within bounds; owner and contact present and well-formed; description present; deprecations carry a `sunset` date; consistent naming between tenant id and file name.

**`gwlint` CLI** (Go, same repo): `gwlint validate <file|dir>` prints a human report (rule id, YAML line, why, how to fix) or `--json`; exit code **0** pass, **1** violations, **2** invalid YAML/schema. `gwlint --fix <file>` writes a corrected file for the mechanically fixable rules and lists the ones that need a human. Golden tests: one good tenant config; several bad ones each triggering specific rules; a `--fix` round-trip test.

`examples/`: `lumen-pay.good.yaml`, `lumen-pay.bad.yaml` (at least 5 violations: a wildcard CORS with credentials, an http upstream, an inlined API key, a missing rate limit, an `/admin` route), and the README that tells a tenant how to onboard (fork/branch → add `tenants/<tenant>.yaml` → open a PR → BOSS validates).
Clean, idiomatic Go; `go vet` and `go test ./...` clean; `make test`, `make run-staging`, `make run-prod`.
A README with: what it is, a 5-minute quick start, the YAML reference, the rulebook table (generated from the YAML), and how `gwlint` is meant to run in CI/BOSS.
Plain, concise naming. Someone at the customer will read this code.
No external services required to run the demo.
`go test -race ./...` passes on the config-swap/reload package.
No secret substring appears in any `gwlint` output, human or `--json` (golden test).
`/readyz` returns the correct boolean in all three internal states, with the rejected-reload case logged.

answers.evidence: JWT/OAuth2 (issuer/audience/scopes, `internal/auth/jwt.go:VerifyJWT`), JWKS caching (`internal/auth/jwks.go:JWKSCache.Get/fetch`), hashed API keys (`internal/auth/apikey.go`, constant-time compare), and mTLS (`internal/auth/mtls.go:VerifyClientCert`, wired via `handler.go:authenticate`) are all real and wired. But "no auth is a config error unless `public:true` with a reason" is only half-enforced: `internal/config/loader.go:validateTenant` rejects no-auth-and-not-public, but never checks for a `public_reason` — that half exists only in `internal/lint/rules.go:47` (gwlint), not in the runtime

`internal/ratelimit/bucket.go:Bucket.Allow` (real token bucket, rps+burst). Keyed independently per tenant (`"tenant:"+ID`) and per tenant+route (`"route:"+ID+"|"+Path`) at `internal/proxy/handler.go:139-163`, reading `config/tenants/lumen-pay.yaml` `rate_limit` blocks.

CORS per route: `internal/proxy/handler.go:applyCORS` reading `m.Route.CORS`, with wildcard+credentials refused at `handler.go:255-257`. Size limits: `handler.go:115-119` `http.MaxBytesReader` using `m.Route.MaxBodyBytes`. Request validation: `internal/validate/jsonschema.go:Against`, LOADED BY `internal/config/types.go` field `Route.RequestSchema` (`yaml:"request_schema"`), read by `internal/config/loader.go:Load` and enforced at `internal/proxy/handler.go:370-376`.

answers.evidence: Timeout: `handler.go:60,352-355`. Retry+backoff for idempotent methods only: `handler.go:292-298 isIdempotent` + `378-410` retry loop. Circuit breaker state machine: `handler.go:301-338 breakerFor/breakerAllows/breakerRecord`, gated at `handler.go:341`.

Header add/remove/rename: `internal/proxy/handler.go:432-445 applyHeaderTransforms`, correct. Request-id propagation has a real bug: `ServeHTTP` mints `reqID` (handler.go:92) and sets it on the response header (93) and in the deferred access log (97), but `proxy()` mints a **second, different** `reqID` (handler.go:351) that overwrites the client-facing header (412) and is sent upstream (396) — so the ID in the access log never matches the ID actually returned to the client or forwarded upstream, defeating request-id correlation.

JSON access logs: `internal/proxy/handler.go:logAccess` (173-201, real `encoding/json.Marshal`). PII redaction: `internal/redact/redact.go:RedactFields`, field list LOADED BY `config/tenants/lumen-pay.yaml` `pii_fields` → `internal/config/types.go:TenantConfig.PIIFields` → wired via `cmd/northgate-gateway/main.go:52-61 proxy.SetPIIFieldsLookup` → `handler.go:181-184`. `/healthz`, `/readyz`: `main.go:64-76`. Prometheus `/metrics`: `internal/metrics/metrics.go:Registry.Render` + `middleware.go:RenderMetricsHandler`, registered `main.go:77-79`.

`docker-compose.yml`: `gateway-staging`/`gateway-production` build the identical `Dockerfile`, differing only in `PORT`/`CONFIG_DIR` env vars; `mock-upstream-staging`/`-production` from `mocks/echo-upstream/main.go` (real JWKS+demo-token+echo server, no external calls).

Unit tests: `internal/proxy/router_test.go` (routing), `internal/auth/auth_test.go` (auth), `internal/ratelimit/limiter_test.go` (rate limits), `internal/config/atomic_test.go`/`reload_metrics_test.go` (reload). Integration: `cmd/northgate-gateway/integration_test.go` builds the real binary and exercises auth → rate limit → upstream (`TestGateway_ValidJWT_ReachesUpstream`, `TestGateway_RateLimit_11thRequestIs429`).

answers.evidence: every listed sub-check is a real, independently-firing rule in `internal/lint/rules.go`: `auth-required` (incl. `public_reason`), `cors-no-wildcard-with-credentials`, `upstream-https-required`, `no-inlined-secrets`, `rate-limit-required` (presence + bounds ≤10000), `no-sensitive-paths-exposed` (`/admin`,`/internal`,`/debug`), `jwt-audience-required`, `mtls-required-partner-sensitive`, `request-size-capped`, `pii-fields-declared`, `no-wildcard-methods`.

`internal/lint/rules.go`: `versioned-base-path`, `kebab-case-path`, `allowed-methods-only`, `timeout-within-bounds`, `owner-present`, `contact-well-formed`, `description-present`, `deprecation-sunset-date`, and `tenant-id-matches-filename` enforced in `internal/lint/engine.go:ValidateDoc:31-37`.

Golden tests in `cmd/gwlint/gwlint_test.go` and `schema_alltenants_test.go` cover good config, multiple bad-triggering-specific-rules, and the fix round-trip.

`go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` both clean (verified live). `Makefile`: `test`, `run-staging`, `run-prod` all present and correctly wired (`test` depends on `vet`, runs `go test ./...` then `-race` on `internal/config`).
